history.dynasty: Jain lay patrons, Śvetāmbara Tapa Gaccha
history.period: Origins 3rd century CE (traditional); present temple renovated 15th century; mulnayak consecrated Vikram Samvat 1429 / 1373 AD
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - Jain (Śvetāmbara) tirth; keep-or-drop decision needed. The ancient tirth was known as Virampur/Viramapura/Nagara; tradition says brothers Virsen and Nakorsen built it in the 3rd century CE and Acharya Sthulibhadra installed the idol. When Alamshah attacked in Vikram Samvat 1280 (1224 AD) the idol was hidden at Kalidrah village; it was brought back and reconsecrated in VS 1429 (1373 AD). About 246 inscriptions record rebuilding over the centuries. Nakoda Bhairava, the miracle-working guardian deity, was installed by Acharya Kirtiratna Suri in VS 1511. DISTRICT FLAG: CSV town/state row says 'Barmer', but Nakoda (Mewa Nagar) now lies in BALOTRA district, carved out of Barmer in August 2023 - documented with the current district.

name: Nakoda Jain Temple
town_description: Nakoda, recorded as Mewa Nagar, is a village about 13 km from Balotra in the forested Aravalli foothills of western Rajasthan. Named after the Jain tirth (earlier called Nagara, Viramapura and Maheva), it functions almost as a pilgrim township during festivals.

travel.road: Set between the villages of Vikrampura and Nakoda, in forest-covered hills; about 13 km from Balotra town (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Posh Dashmi fair in Poush month (December-January).
visitor_information.opening_hours: No published hours found (verify) - Jain temples typically open morning to evening.
